articles.title: Starlink Signal Leakage Threatens Radio Astronomy's Most Critical Frequencies
articles.summary: Starlink's signal leakage is threatening radio astronomy's most critical frequencies, with the company's hardware emitting up to 10,000 times stronger signals than the cosmic signals it's supposed to detect. Researchers found 112,534 individual radio emissions from 1,806 unique Starlink satellites across 73-235 MHz frequency range, with some satellites emitting periodic 13-kHz tones at 137 MHz every 100 seconds. The findings, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, indicate that the signal leakage is up to 10 million times stronger than the cosmic signals SKA-Low is built to detect, and could potentially interfere with early-universe hydrogen signals.
